answer_1.quote: Natural Language Generation (NLG) has long been crucial in natural language processing research, encompassing common tasks such as text summarization and dialogue response generation.
answer_1.outputs: The outputs include summaries in text summarization and responses in dialogue generation, which are evaluated for quality using various metrics and human judgments.

answer_2.quote: Traditional metrics primarily include string matching-based methods, such as BLEU and ROUGE, as well as semantic representation-based methods like BERTScore and BARTScore.

answer_3.quote: Recently, large language models (LLMs) such as have demonstrated remarkable leaps in text comprehension and instruction-following capabilities. As a result, many studies have shifted their focus to leveraging carefully designed instructions to directly prompt LLMs for simulating human evaluation.
methods: scoring each target separately and comparing scores

answer_4.quote: We responsibly recruit annotators who have a good command of English from local universities for our human evaluation and provide reasonable payment for their work.
answer_4.guideline: The evaluation results of each target t_ij from humans (h_ij) or metrics (x_ij). More specifically, the results from humans are usually presented in the form of discrete ratings based on the evaluation scale and may involve multiple annotators.
